domain_entities.name: LeaveRequest
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee's request for leave. Tracks the full lifecycle from draft through submission, approval/rejection, and cancellation. References the employee, the leave policy, and the approving manager.

domain_entities.name: LeavePolicy
domain_entities.purpose: Defines the rules and entitlements for a specific category of leave. Governs how many days an employee is entitled to, accrual behaviour, notice requirements, and whether manager approval is mandatory.

domain_entities.name: LeaveBalance
domain_entities.purpose: Tracks an employee's leave entitlement, usage, and remaining balance for a specific leave policy within a fiscal year. Updated atomically when leave is approved or cancelled.

domain_entities.name: Employee
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee in the organisation. Owns leave balances and submits leave requests. Has a reporting manager who approves/rejects requests.

domain_entities.name: LeaveType
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of leave categories. Each LeavePolicy is associated with exactly one LeaveType. The feature scope covers annual, sick, and emergency; the remaining types are defined for completeness.

domain_entities.name: LeaveRequestStatus
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of states a LeaveRequest passes through during its lifecycle. Governs which transitions are valid and which actors may initiate them.

domain_entities.name: BalanceStatus
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of LeaveBalance states. ACTIVE means the balance can be drawn against. EXHAUSTED means remainingDays is zero. FROZEN means the balance is temporarily locked.

domain_entities.name: EmploymentStatus
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of employee employment states. Determines eligibility for leave requests and balance accrual.

domain_entities.name: AuditLog
domain_entities.purpose: Immutable record of every state-changing operation across the leave management module. Satisfies GP-002 (audit trail).

domain_entities.name: Notification
domain_entities.purpose: Represents a notification sent to an employee (e.g., leave submitted, approved, rejected, cancelled, balance low). Persisted for in-app notification history.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 1 — Foundation: Enums, Models, and Shared Infrastructure
recommended_phases.rationale: Zero-dependency leaf modules first. leave-type (enum), leave-status (enum + transition rules), and the shared db connection / base repository are already in place. Add the audit module (model + repository + service) since it has no domain dependencies and is needed by everything else. Add the employee module (model + repository + service) — depends only on audit. Create tables: employee, audit_log.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2 — Policy & Balance Domain Services
recommended_phases.rationale: leave-policy depends only on leave-type (Phase 1). leave-balance depends on leave-type, leave-policy, employee, and audit (all Phase 1). Build repositories, service interfaces, and service implementations for both. Create tables: leave_policy, leave_balance.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3 — Notification Module
recommended_phases.rationale: notification depends only on employee (Phase 1). Build the notification model, repository, service interface, and service implementation. Create table: notification.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4 — Leave Request Orchestration & API Surface
recommended_phases.rationale: leave-request depends on everything above. Build the LeaveRequest model, repository, service interface, service implementation (orchestrates policy checks, balance validation/deduction, audit recording, and notifications), controller, route definitions, and input validation schemas. Create table: leave_request.

architecture_md_update:
## Leave Management Module

### Overview

The leave management module enables employees to apply for annual, sick, and emergency leave, managers to approve or reject requests, and the system to track leave balances. It is built as a modular monolith using TypeScript, Fastify, React Native, and PostgreSQL, following the principles in GOLDEN_PRINCIPLES.md.

### Domain Entities

| Entity | Purpose | Lifecycle States |
|--------|---------|------------------|
| **LeaveRequest** | Employee leave application. Tracks full lifecycle from draft to cancellation. | DRAFT → SUBMITTED → (APPROVED \| REJECTED) → CANCELLED. CANCELLED reachable from DRAFT, SUBMITTED, or APPROVED. APPROVED → CANCELLED triggers balance restoration. |
| **LeavePolicy** | Rules and entitlements for a leave category. | ACTIVE → INACTIVE → ARCHIVED. Only ACTIVE policies accept new requests. |
| **LeaveBalance** | Employee entitlement, usage, and remaining days per policy per fiscal year. | ACTIVE → EXHAUSTED (auto when remainingDays=0) → ACTIVE (auto when remainingDays>0). ACTIVE → FROZEN (admin action only, manual revert). |
| **Employee** | Organisation employee who owns balances and submits requests. | ACTIVE → INACTIVE → TERMINATED. Only ACTIVE employees may submit leave requests. Termination auto-cancels SUBMITTED requests. |
| **LeaveType** | Enum: annual, sick, emergency, unpaid, maternity, paternity. | N/A |
| **LeaveRequestStatus** | Enum: DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED. | N/A |
| **BalanceStatus** | Enum: ACTIVE, EXHAUSTED, FROZEN. | N/A |
| **EmploymentStatus** | Enum: ACTIVE, INACTIVE, TERMINATED. | N/A |
| **AuditLog** | Immutable record of state-changing operations (GP-002). | N/A |
| **Notification** | Persisted notification for employees (submitted, approved, rejected, cancelled, balance low). | N/A |

### Business Rules

- **BR-001** Date validation: startDate ≤ endDate, both in future at submission, total days ≤ remainingDays.
- **BR-002** Manager approval: approvedBy must match employee's managerId; self-approval prohibited.
- **BR-003** Balance deduction on approval: atomic increment of usedDays, decrement of remainingDays.
- **BR-004** Balance restoration on cancellation of APPROVED request.
- **BR-005** Minimum notice period enforced at submission (unless emergency leave).
- **BR-006** Only ACTIVE policies may be used.
- **BR-007** Only ACTIVE employees may submit; termination auto-cancels SUBMITTED requests.
- **BR-008** Overlap prevention: no overlapping APPROVED/SUBMITTED requests for same employee and leave type.
- **BR-009** Fiscal year scoping: deduction applied to fiscal year of startDate; no negative remainingDays.
- **BR-010** Valid state transitions: DRAFT→SUBMITTED (employee), SUBMITTED→APPROVED/REJECTED (manager), SUBMITTED→CANCELLED (employee), APPROVED→CANCELLED (employee), DRAFT→CANCELLED (employee).
- **BR-011** Emergency leave bypasses minimum notice.
- **BR-012** Balance status auto-transition: EXHAUSTED when remainingDays=0, ACTIVE when >0; FROZEN only by admin.

### Module Boundaries

```
src/modules/
├── leave-type/          # LeaveType enum, constants
├── leave-status/        # LeaveRequestStatus enum, transition rules
├── leave-policy/        # LeavePolicy model, repository, service
├── leave-balance/       # LeaveBalance model, BalanceStatus enum, repository, service
├── leave-request/       # LeaveRequest model, repository, service, controller, routes, validation
├── employee/            # Employee model, EmploymentStatus enum, repository, service
├── audit/               # AuditLog model, repository, service
└── notification/        # Notification model, repository, service
```

### Dependency Direction

```
leave-request ──→ leave-balance ──→ leave-policy ──→ leave-type
    │                  │
    │                  └──→ employee ──→ audit
    │                  └──→ audit
    │
    ├──→ leave-status (leaf)
    ├──→ leave-type (leaf)
    ├──→ leave-policy ──→ leave-type
    ├──→ employee ──→ audit
    ├──→ audit (leaf)
    └──→ notification ──→ employee ──→ audit
```

All arrows point inward. No cycles.

### Conceptual Tables

| Table | Key Fields | Index Rationale |
|-------|------------|-----------------|
| **leave_request** | id, employee_id, leave_policy_id, start_date, end_date, status, approved_by | employee_id (my requests), status (approval queues), leave_policy_id (type filter), approved_by (manager queue), start_date/end_date (calendar, overlap) |
| **leave_balance** | id, employee_id, leave_policy_id, fiscal_year, remaining_days, status | employee_id (per-employee lookup), leave_policy_id (policy filter), fiscal_year (scoping), unique(employee_id, leave_policy_id, fiscal_year) |
| **leave_policy** | id, leave_type, is_active | leave_type (filter by type), is_active (active policies only) |
| **employee** | id, email, employee_number, manager_id, employment_status | email (unique login), employee_number (unique HR), manager_id (team queries), employment_status (eligibility) |
| **audit_log** | id, entity_type, entity_id, action, performed_by, performed_at | (entity_type, entity_id) (entity trail), performed_by (actor trail), performed_at (time range), action (action type) |
| **notification** | id, recipient_employee_id, is_read, created_at | recipient_employee_id (user inbox), is_read (unread filter), created_at (ordering) |

### Service Interfaces

- **ILeavePolicyService**: getPolicyById, getPolicyByLeaveType, getActivePolicies, getEntitlementDays, requiresManagerApproval, getMinimumNoticeDays
- **ILeaveBalanceService**: getBalance, getAllBalances, hasSufficientBalance, deductBalance, restoreBalance, initializeBalance, recalculateBalance
- **ILeaveRequestService**: submitLeaveRequest, approveLeaveRequest, rejectLeaveRequest, cancelLeaveRequest, getLeaveRequestById, getLeaveRequestsByEmployee, getPendingLeaveRequests, getTeamLeaveRequests, validateLeaveRequest
- **IEmployeeService**: getEmployeeById, getManagerId, isActive, getTeamMembers
- **IAuditService**: recordCreate, recordUpdate, recordApprove, recordReject, recordCancel
- **INotificationService**: notifyLeaveSubmitted, notifyLeaveApproved, notifyLeaveRejected, notifyLeaveCancelled, notifyBalanceLow

### Implementation Phases

1. **Foundation**: leave-type, leave-status, audit, employee modules + tables (employee, audit_log).
2. **Policy & Balance**: leave-policy, leave-balance modules + tables (leave_policy, leave_balance).
3. **Notification**: notification module + table (notification).
4. **Leave Request Orchestration**: leave-request module + table (leave_request), controller, routes, validation.

### Stack Compliance

- Language: TypeScript (strict mode)
- Runtime: Node.js 20
- Framework: Fastify (REST API)
- Frontend: React Native (mobile client)
- Database: PostgreSQL (via pg Pool at src/shared/db/connection.ts)
- Architecture: modular-monolith with clear module boundaries and dependency inversion (interfaces)
- Testing: Jest
- Package manager: npm

All repositories implement interfaces (GP-001). All state-changing operations are audited (GP-002). Input validation is enforced at the controller layer (GP-003). RBAC is enforced at route level (GP-005). Transactions are used for atomic balance updates (GP-004).
sql_schemas: table leave_request | fields: id, employee_id, leave_policy_id, start_date, end_date, reason, status, approved_by, approved_at, rejection_reason, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employee.id; leave_policy_id -> leave_policy.id; approved_by -> employee.id | indexes: employee_id: frequent lookups for 'my leave requests' per employee; status: filtering by status for approval queues and dashboards; leave_policy_id: filtering requests by leave type; approved_by: manager approval queue lookups; start_date, end_date: date-range queries for calendar views and overlap detection

table leave_balance | fields: id, employee_id, leave_policy_id, total_entitlement, used_days, remaining_days, fiscal_year, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employee.id; leave_policy_id -> leave_policy.id | indexes: employee_id: per-employee balance lookups on every leave request; leave_policy_id: filtering balances by policy type; fiscal_year: partition-like access pattern — balances are always scoped to a fiscal year; employee_id, leave_policy_id, fiscal_year: unique constraint enforcement for one balance row per employee/policy/year

table leave_policy | fields: id, policy_name, leave_type, entitlement_days, accrual_rate, max_accumulation, minimum_notice_days, requires_manager_approval, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | indexes: leave_type: filtering active policies by leave type when employees apply; is_active: filtering only active policies for employee-facing queries

table employee | fields: id, employee_number, first_name, last_name, email, manager_id, department, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at | pk: id | fks: manager_id -> employee.id | indexes: email: unique lookup for login and identity resolution; employee_number: unique lookup for HR operations; manager_id: team-level queries for manager dashboards; employment_status: filtering active employees for leave eligibility

table audit_log | fields: id, entity_type, entity_id, action, old_values, new_values, performed_by, performed_at, ip_address, user_agent, created_at | pk: id | fks: performed_by -> employee.id | indexes: entity_type, entity_id: audit trail lookups for a specific entity; performed_by: audit trail filtered by actor; performed_at: time-range audit queries; action: filtering audit records by action type (APPROVE, REJECT, etc.)

table notification | fields: id, recipient_employee_id, type, title, message, is_read, related_entity_type, related_entity_id, created_at | pk: id | fks: recipient_employee_id -> employee.id | indexes: recipient_employee_id: fetch all notifications for a user; is_read: filter unread notifications; created_at: order notifications by recency
